segments.dry: Reviewers with dry skin, including some who also describe it as acne-prone or dehydrated, report the pads brighten and reduce dark spots without drying the skin further, and several say they got no breakouts using it daily.
segments.sensitive: Most reviewers with sensitive skin, including some with a history of hyperpigmentation or scarring, report no stinging, burning, or irritation even with daily use; however, reviewers with rosacea report the opposite — flushing, irritation, and no visible results for one, and an unlisted BHA that made another avoid repurchasing — and a third with sensitive, scar-prone skin found it dried her skin out.
segments.combination: Reviewers with combination skin, including some with an oily T-zone, report the pads brighten and help control shine in oilier areas without irritating the rest of the face; complaints from this group are about messy or flimsy packaging rather than the formula itself.

concerns.aging: Several reviewers report visibly reduced under-eye puffiness, fine lines, and a firmer look, in some cases after a single use; however, one reviewer specifically notes she didn't see a meaningful difference in elasticity or firmness.
concerns.dehydration: Most reviewers report the pads are hydrating rather than drying, some noting the moisture lasts well beyond the recommended wear time; however, a few reviewers, including two who describe their skin as sensitive or compromised, report the opposite — increased dryness, tightness, or a disrupted skin barrier.
concerns.redness: Reviewers dealing with redness around the nose and cheeks report it looks calmer within days of starting use; however, one reviewer with rosacea-prone skin reports the pads flushed her cheeks and irritated her skin instead.
concerns.barrier: One reviewer credits consistent niacinamide use with supporting her skin barrier, but another reports the opposite — that this formula left her barrier feeling disrupted, with increased dryness and new sun sensitivity even under sunscreen.
concerns.spots: The large majority of reviewers, including several targeting dark spots, post-acne marks, melasma, or under-eye discoloration, report gradual fading and a more even tone within one to four weeks; however, at least three reviewers saw no noticeable brightening or evening at all despite weeks of consistent use.
concerns.blemishes: Reviewers with acne-prone skin generally report the pads don't trigger breakouts and, for some, help calm existing acne and fade post-acne marks; one reviewer with rosacea-adjacent skin, however, reports still getting pimples and blackheads with no improvement after using half the jar.
concerns.oiliness: Reviewers who mention oiliness, particularly in the T-zone, report the pads help control shine and balance oil production.

extraits.titre: Not really for my skin type
extraits.texte: I really wanted to love the Anua Niacinamide 5 TXA Brightening Pads, but unfortunately they didn't work well for my skin. I used them consistently for several weeks with the hope of improving my hyperpigmentation, and I didn't see any noticeable brightening or evening of my skin tone. Instead, my skin became increasingly dry and sensitive. I also noticed that my skin felt more reactive to sunlight, even while wearing sunscreen, which was concerning. The formula containing 5% niacinamide and tranexamic acid may work for some, but for me it disrupted my skin barrier rather than supporting it. If you have sensitive or already compromised skin, this may be something to approach with caution. While the concept is great, this product just wasn't a good match for my skin and didn't deliver the brightening results I was hoping for. Incentive Review
